title: Connectivity compatibility categorizer and deployment fastpath for private onramp requests
creator: Avery Chen
description: Summary: Build a reusable taxonomy and automated compatibility scorer that routes incoming Private/VPC/on‑prem customer requests into a Fastpath (self-serve or concierge) or Remediation lane. The goal is to reduce mean triage time for network-limited onramp requests, lower engineering touch for low-risk customers, and provide clear remediation artifacts and templates for blockers (proxy, firewall rules, NAT, cert pinning, egress allowlists, kernel modules).
acceptance_criteria: Taxonomy: A documented compatibility taxonomy covering >90% of past 12 months network-related private/onprem requests (categories: direct-https, proxy-required, port-restricted, airgap-only, outbound-restricted, MTU/fragmentation, custom DNS/NTP/PKI).
Scorer: Automated probe + questionnaire produces a deterministic readiness score (0-100) and recommended lane (fastpath/remediate) for a given customer within 10 minutes of intake.
Coverage: The taxonomy + automated scorer must match historical human triage decision in >=95% of a 200-sample audit or produce a documented reason for divergence.
Fastpath SLA: For requests flagged Fastpath, average triage-to-activation time <= 3 business days and >60% of fastpath trials proceed without ENG intervention.
Runbooks: Runbooks and templated comms (preflight checklist, proxy sample, firewall rule snippets, cert instructions) published in Confluence and linked from intake email templates.
Integration: Intake form fields added to Zendesk/Support Intake and reflected as structured metadata in Linear so routing/metrics are captured.
Observability: Dashboard in Console showing intake throughput, fastpath conversion rate, common blockers and time-to-resolution by category.
Stakeholder signoff: Security, Solutions, and Infra teams approve final taxonomy and probe scripts prior to rollout.
tasks: Audit historical tickets: sample 200 private/VPC/onprem requests from last 12 months and extract blocker signals (owner: PM)
Draft taxonomy: produce initial compatibility tree and mapping to remediation artifacts (owner: PM + Solutions)

Probe library: Implement 6 lightweight probes (TLS handshake, proxy traversal, egress port check, DNS resolution pattern, MTU test, cert chain health) as scripts + Docker image for customers to run in their environment (owner: ENG infra)
Intake UX: Add structured fields to intake form (network topology, egress policy, proxy type, cert mgmt) and quick-score feedback for customers (owner: Design + PM)
Automated scorer: Small service to combine questionnaire + probe results into readiness score with explanation text (owner: ENG - integrations)
Runbooks & comms: Author Confluence pages, email templates, and Solutions playbook for remediation lanes (owner: SolutionsEng)
Integrations: Wire up intake -> Linear tags and Console dashboard metrics (owner: ENG - observability)
Pilot: Run pilot with 5 incoming customer requests and measure fastpath conversion and ENG touches (owner: PM)
Postmortem & iteration: Collect pilot feedback, adjust taxonomy/scorer, and expand probes as needed (owner: PM + ENG)
Security review: Submit probe code and scoring logic for security review and signoff (owner: Security)
Docs & SDK: Ship a small CLI that runs probes and outputs JSON for intake attachments (owner: Developer Experience)
decisions: Start with a deterministic scorer (rule-based) rather than ML to ensure explainability for customers and security review.
Probe runs will be optional for customers; system can accept questionnaire-only but will flag reduced confidence.

Fastpath criteria will require at minimum: outbound HTTPS allowed, no deep cert pinning, reachable KMS endpoint if using HSM, and non-airgapped control-plane connectivity unless using a documented bridge pattern.
open_questions: What success threshold should classify a request as Fastpath for enterprise customers (suggested: >=85)?
Should we allow Solutions team to manually override lane decisions in Linear, and how to capture audit trail?
Do we require probe artifacts to be uploaded, or is an ephemeral signed result sufficient for compliance?
Can we reuse existing network probe code from onboarding-scripts repo, or must this live in a separate repo with stricter review?
How will we handle customers that pass probes but declare internal policy reasons that require remediation lane?
